titulo: Key image first: cARCKHÉtic still and lookbook
lead: Before you animate, get the picture right. An image takes seconds, so you can test the look many times and take only the approved frame into video. The lookbook keeps the recipe for that look in a base prompt that goes into every still of the scene unchanged.
objetivo: build the scene's lookbook and generate the stills for the key shots before any video, using the same base prompt.

aprende.t: Why the key image comes before the video
The ingredients of a look, described without a director's name
A base prompt that repeats in every still
Image generators in Oct 2026, closed and open

hero_alt: A printed photograph pinned to a clothesline inside a dark room, showing the inside of a bakery at dawn with the oven lit and steam rising.

secoes.sub: Five steps, in this order. Click each one.

nos.detalhe: Choose the shots that define the scene: usually the first, the turning point, and the last. In the batch: 1 (dark street), 4 (oven opening), and 8 (iron door).
Palette, lens, light, texture, and aspect ratio, written once. They become the base prompt.
The look text, identical in every still. Only the subject and the action of each shot change.
Generate a few versions of each key shot. Compare them side by side: the look has to be the same in all three.
The chosen still goes into the folder with the shot number. In lesson 4, it is the first frame of the video.

secoes.legenda: If the look changes from one still to another, the problem is in the base prompt, not in the generator: adjust the recipe and generate again.

texto: Getting the look wrong in a video costs a whole generation. In an image, you change the light, the lens, and the palette in minutes and compare them side by side.
The approved frame is the anchor of the scene: it carries the character, the place, the palette, and the light. Everything that comes after inherits from it.
Palette (two or three dominant colors), lens (wide-angle, normal, or tele), light (from the look card in course 0), texture (film grain, contrast), and aspect ratio of the frame.
Describe the ingredient, don't name a director or a film: "in the style of so-and-so" imitates a real person's work and changes depending on how the generator understands the name.

exemplo.texto: night blue on the street, tile white, orange only in the fire; 35 mm; low-key with side light from the oven; fine grain; 16:9

texto: Put the ingredients together in one line that goes into every still the same way. Leave a marked space for what changes from shot to shot: the subject and the action.
If the generator accepts a style reference image, use the first approved still as the reference for the others (lesson 5 goes deeper).

Open: FLUX.2 [klein] (Jan/2026). The 4B is Apache 2.0 and runs on about 8 GB of VRAM; the 9B has a non-commercial license. It generates, edits, and accepts multiple reference images, according to the official repository.

Closed: Midjourney V8.1 came out on 04/30/2026, according to its documentation. GPT Image 2 and Nano Banana Pro are cited by third-party sites as strong in 2026, with no official confirmation checked here.

exemplo.texto: Official FLUX.2 repository on GitHub (checked on 10/19/2026).

secoes.sub: The lookbook that the page checks and the request for the AI assistant to build the base prompt.

blocos.conteudo:
Palette: <2 or 3 dominant colors and where they appear>
Lens: <wide-angle, 35 mm, 50 mm, tele; shallow or deep focus>
Light: <your look card from course 0>
Texture: <grain, contrast, sharpness>
Aspect ratio: <16:9, 9:16, 2.39:1...>
Base prompt: <everything above in one line, with [SUBJECT AND ACTION] in place of what changes>
Key shots: <numbers of the shots that become stills>

blocos.rot: Request to the AI assistant (base prompt)
blocos.conteudo:
You are a cARCKHÉtographer. With the look card and the character sheet below, write a cARCKHÉtic image base prompt, in one line, to repeat in every still of the scene.
Rules:
- describe palette, lens, light, texture, and aspect ratio with concrete words;
- do not name a director, film, photographer, or brand;
- leave the [SUBJECT AND ACTION] placeholder where what changes from shot to shot goes.
Look card:
<paste the look.txt here>
Character sheet:
<paste the ficha.txt here>

secoes.sub: Paste the lookbook.txt (or upload the file). Test first with the two examples.
secoes.rot: Paste your lookbook.txt here (one line per ingredient):

grupos.rot: the aspect ratio of the frame (e.g., 16:9)

secoes.exemplo:
Palette: night blue on the street, white tile, orange only in the oven fire
Lens: 35 mm, shallow focus on the close-ups
Light: low-key, side light from the oven, steam in the beam; cold, dark street
Texture: fine film grain, soft contrast
Aspect ratio: 16:9
Base prompt: cARCKHÉ photograph in a neighborhood bakery at 4:50 a.m., 35 mm, low-key with side light from the oven, white tile, night-blue street through the window, fine film grain, 16:9, [SUBJECT AND ACTION]
Key shots: 1 (dark street), 4 (oven opening), 8 (iron door)
secoes.exemplo_errado:
Palette: warm
Lens: cARCKHÉtic
Light: style of a famous director
Base prompt: beautiful bakery, cARCKHÉtic, 8k

exercicios.titulo: Lookbook · the recipe for your scene
exercicios.texto: Fill in the lookbook.txt using the template, with no director, film, or brand names. Pick three key shots from your shot list. Paste it into "Check your lookbook" and download the file to the project folder.
exercicios.pronto: the page answers OK: lookbook with 7 fields and the lookbook.txt is in the project folder.

exercicios.texto: In whatever image generator you have (open or closed), generate the three key shots with the same base prompt, changing only the [SUBJECT AND ACTION]. Save the approved one for each with the shot number: plano-01, plano-04, plano-08.
exercicios.pronto: the project folder has the three image files with the shot number in the name, and the prompt for each one starts with the same Base prompt from the lookbook.txt.

secoes.sub: Four questions. The explanation shows up after each answer.

perguntas.p: Why generate the key image before the video?
opcoes: Because video generators only accept starting from an image.
Because testing the look on an image is fast, and the approved frame becomes an anchor.
Because the generated image always comes out at a higher resolution than the video generated afterward.
Because video generated from plain text comes out without audio.
perguntas.explica: An image takes seconds: you can make mistakes and fix light, lens, and palette several times. The approved frame carries the look and, in lesson 4, becomes the first frame of the video. Video from text also exists, and it also has audio.

perguntas.p: Which line describes a look without depending on a person's name?
opcoes: "In the style of a famous director of symmetrical films."
"Like the cARCKHÉtography of that sci-fi movie everyone knows."
"Night blue and white, 35 mm, low-key, fine grain, 16:9."
perguntas.explica: A described ingredient works in any generator and doesn't imitate anyone's work. A director's or film's name depends on how each generator understands the name, and it copies a signature that isn't yours.

perguntas.p: The three stills came out with different colors. Where do you tweak first?
opcoes: In the base prompt: some ingredient of the look is vague or missing.
In the resolution: larger stills come out with steadier color.
In the generator: switch tools for each still until the colors match.
In the edit: fixing the color afterward always solves the difference.
perguntas.explica: If the base prompt is identical and concrete, the look tends to repeat. A vague palette ("warm") lets each generation pick for itself. Color correction in post exists (course 2), but it won't save a still with different light.

perguntas.p: You want to generate stills on your own machine and use them in paid work. Which option from the lesson fits?
opcoes: FLUX.2 [klein] 9B, because it's the biggest in the klein family.
Any open model, because open always allows commercial use.
A closed generator, because only closed allows paid work.
FLUX.2 [klein] 4B, which is Apache 2.0 and runs on about 8 GB.
perguntas.explica: In the klein family, the 4B is Apache 2.0 and the 9B has a non-commercial license. "Open" says the weights are available, not what you're allowed to do with them: read each one's license.

itens.texto: Nail the look on the still; the approved one becomes the first frame of the video.
Palette, lens, light, texture and aspect ratio, with no director or film named.
Same in every still; only the subject and the action change.
